svg.title: 3. Service-to-service: VPC Lattice and PrivateLink
svg.text: Service auth policy (fine-grained, owned by payments)
Service-to-service with identity: VPC Lattice auth policies inside the bank, PrivateLink to a partner, endpoint policies for AWS APIs
shared with the org via RAM
1. resolves tokenizer.bank.internal to a link-local address
2. checks the SigV4 signature and the network policy
3. checks the service policy (both must allow)
4. forwards to a healthy target in the payments VPC
5. writes an access log: caller ARN, path, status
No TGW hop, no route tables, no CIDR overlap issue.
Access logs to Security Lake. Allowed and denied
calls both show the caller role ARN.
Credentials from outside the org are
refused at this endpoint, and our own
roles cannot reach secrets in another
AWS PrivateLink, TCP 443, one direction only
Only our account is an allowed principal on the
endpoint service. No peering, no route tables,
no CIDR coordination, and the bureau cannot
open a connection back into the CDE.
